PullRequest.Title: Suggest scoped terminal auto-approve rules for pnpm and bun
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #347359

When an agent runs a pnpm or bun command in the terminal, the approval dropdown only offers "Allow `pnpm …`" (every pnpm command) or the exact command line. npm and yarn get a scoped rule such as `npm run lint` or `npx eslint`.

### Change

`suggestAutoApproveRuleKeys` now treats `pnpm`, `bun` and `bunx` like `npm`, `npx` and `yarn`:

| Command | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm run lint src/a.ts` | `pnpm` | `pnpm run lint` |
| `pnpm exec eslint src/a.ts` | `pnpm` | `pnpm exec eslint` |
| `pnpm eslint src/a.ts` | `pnpm` | `pnpm eslint` |
| `bun run test src/a.ts` | `bun` | `bun run test` |
| `bunx eslint src/a.ts` | `bunx` | `bunx eslint` |
| bare `pnpm`, `bun`, `bunx` | `pnpm`, `bun`, `bunx` | no rule offered, as for bare `npm`, `yarn` and `git` today |

`pnpm exec`, `pnpm dlx` and `bun x` are sub-sub-commands like `npm run`, so the suggested rule names the tool rather than approving every executable. `pnpm --dir <path> …` isn't covered: skipping option values would need per-tool knowledge of which options take one.

For a bare tool name, neither a prefix rule nor an exact-command rule is offered. That's how `npm`, `yarn` and `git` already behave: a `pnpm` rule would approve every pnpm command, which is what this change avoids. Whether bare tool names should get an exact-command option is a separate question that affects all of these tools.

### Testing

New cases in the existing snapshot test, including bare `pnpm`, `bun` and `bunx`.

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/terminal/test/common/autoApprove/suggestAutoApproveRules.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/test/browser/runInTerminalHelpers.test.ts`: **87 passing**.
- With the new cases on origin/main's implementation, the snapshot test **fails**: pnpm and bun get `pnpm` and `bun`.
- `pnpm run oxlint` on both changed files: clean.

This wasn't tested in a live agent session.

🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @aeschli.

Scenarios.Scenario: Build the workbench terminal approval dropdown for an unapproved pnpm, bun, or bunx command, including compound command lines and bare tool names.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CommandLineAutoApproveAnalyzer.analyze first awaits shell parsing and Promise.all of approval checks, then synchronously generates suggestions and confirmation actions before returning the approval UI metadata. The diff changes only the final in-memory suggestion branch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check package.json existence, read its contents, and parse script names when workspace npm-script approval is enabled and a qualifying pnpm script lacks an earlier matching approval rule.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For M qualifying script subcommands with workspace-contained cwd, M existence checks and up to M reads, including repeated checks for the same package.json because this helper does not coalesce them. pnpm exec/dlx built-ins and bun/bunx do not qualify. These checks precede suggestion generation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same pnpm script detection, boundary calls, Promise.all concurrency, and package.json parsing already occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All scheduled approval checks must settle before the dropdown metadata is generated.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Let U be the number of unapproved parsed shell commands and T their total token/text size. Suggestions remain linear in T, with K distinct suggested prefixes after Set deduplication, K <= U. Previously pnpm/bun/bunx suggestions deduplicated by tool name; now distinct scripts/tools can produce distinct keys, while the three scope actions still group all K keys.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing subcommand approval checks run in Promise.all. The changed suggestion map, token scans, deduplication, and action generation execute synchronously once per eligible analyzed command. No new async operations or concurrency are introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The suggestion helper has no cache or persistent per-command state. Its module-level sets gain only eight fixed string entries. Existing parse trees are keyed by language plus command line and cleared after ten seconds of inactivity; the parser is lazy. Optional package.json script checks have no explicit positive, negative, or in-flight cache in NpmScriptAutoApprover. None of these cache behaviors changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the entire helper, both changed sets, the filtering caller, the analyzer's generation gate, and the optional script approval implementation. Existing expensive checks run before the changed helper and receive unchanged inputs.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings were measured. Longer scoped keys and multiple distinct script keys add bounded string/action payload work; realistic command lines do not establish a consequential regression from this change.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This extends an existing linear token-processing branch to three more tools without new boundary calls, scheduling changes, or unbounded retained state. Bare tool names now suppress scoped actions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Construct agent-host shell confirmation options for unapproved package-manager commands.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SessionPermissionManager.createToolReadyAction synchronously evaluates the command and constructs scoped options when an interactive shell confirmation is needed. The helper's output is converted into rule strings and JSON-encoded option IDs before the ready action is returned.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON.stringify each grouped permission-rule array into a confirmation option ID.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two encodings of the K-prefix rule group when nonempty, plus the existing two encodings of the exact-command group when eligible. No serialization call per prefix.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same group-level encodings occurred; pnpm/bun/bunx prefix strings were shorter and collapsed by base-tool name. Exact-command encoding behavior is unchanged except for suppression of bare special tool names.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Encoding must complete before the ready action containing confirmation options can be returned.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize tree-sitter WASM and read bash and PowerShell grammar WASM files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared process-level resource initialization, including two explicit grammar reads; zero additional grammar reads for warm command evaluations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same process-global initialization promise and grammar loading existed before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initialization is a precondition for synchronous command evaluation, not newly awaited by the suggestion helper or by the changed lines.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: U unapproved shell commands and K distinct scoped prefixes, K <= U. The prefix group is encoded twice, once for session and once for host scope; exact-command groups continue to cover U commands. Different pnpm/bun scripts may no longer collapse into a single base-tool key, but the number of grouped options does not increase per script.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Option evaluation and JSON encoding are synchronous. Existing grammar initialization loads the two grammar files concurrently through Promise.allSettled with a shared initialization promise; the diff does not initiate another load or add per-command parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The helper remains stateless. CommandAutoApprover shares a process-global initialization promise, loading WASM resources once, and caches compiled default rules. Warm evaluation uses initialized parser resources. No changed cache keys, misses, invalidation, or initialization ownership.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the direct agent-host caller, ready-action construction, JSON encoding implementation, and shared parser initialization. Neither boundary frequency nor concurrency is changed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Static review establishes slightly larger grouped prefix payloads but not problematic durations or practical large-cardinality inputs. No performance measurements are available.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression. Richer rule prefixes alone do not establish excessive serialization or I/O; group counts and initialization placement remain unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Accept a suggested scoped approval rule and persist it for later terminal commands.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Workbench session grants update in-memory rules; workspace/user grants await one grouped configuration update before completing confirmation. Agent-host session grants dispatch a grouped configuration change; host grants update state immediately and enqueue persistence without awaiting disk completion on the confirmation handler.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the merged terminal auto-approval setting through the existing workspace/user configuration service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configuration update for the selected workspace or user scope, regardless of K keys; zero configuration writes for session scope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One grouped update for the same chosen scope. The diff changes key content and deduplication granularity, not placement or write count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The chosen workspace/user configuration update is awaited before the confirmation handler proceeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For a new host grant, serialize root configuration, mkdir the directory, write a temporary file, and rename it into place.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One queued mkdir/write/rename sequence per changed host grant containing all K new keys; zero writes for an already-present identical grant or absent root persistence resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same deduplicated grouped grant and serialized persistence chain already existed. No per-key write was introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Root JSON serialization occurs synchronously; filesystem work is queued and is not awaited by handleToolCallConfirmed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON.stringify the root configuration snapshot before queuing its write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-root encoding per changed host grant, irrespective of K keys.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same full-root encoding already occurred for each new host grant. Longer suggested key strings do not alter the number of encodings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Encoding occurs synchronously in updateRootConfig; actual disk persistence remains deferred.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K distinct selected prefix keys are merged with R existing rules. A scope action contains all K keys, not K separate persistence requests. Scoped keys can increase the number of intentionally selected rules relative to a broad pnpm/bun grant, but growth requires explicit user grants and remains bounded by selected command prefixes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Workbench workspace/user writes are awaited once per nonempty scope group. Agent-host root writes are chained on _rootConfigWrite, giving one-at-a-time filesystem persistence rather than a per-rule burst. Session updates are synchronous state dispatches.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Workbench settings/session rule stores merge by key. Agent-host session and host permission lists deduplicate using Set and skip updates when no new rules are added. Existing configurations are reused; no new cache or retained history is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the workbench scope grouping, agent-host grant deduplication, session dispatch, and serialized root persistence implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of user-selected scoped grants and existing configuration size are unknown. The changed prefix specificity does not by itself prove unacceptable rule-store growth or costly persistence.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Existing writes stay grouped and host disk concurrency stays serialized; the PR introduces no eager persistence, redundant per-key boundary calls, or automatic unbounded retention.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass for PR #350388 against bb6101481d2b2c08ab730826c4a7a859a6ced0a5. Inspected the complete two-file inventory and all three diff hunks, both production callers, relevant approval checks, grouped rule consumers, parser caching, serialization, and persistence. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue or concrete performance regression fix qualifies for reporting. Review was static and read-only.
